If you should have the opportunity to do business with us, I hope your experience is pleasant and helpful.

FREE ONLINE RECORDS SEARCH
After you have registered to use our FREE site, don't forget to also sign up for FRAUD NOTIFY. A FREE service offered to notify you via email anytime a document is presented and recorded in your name.
Images date back to 1852 but are only indexed from 1922 to present. Indexing pre-1922 is occurring on a regular basis. If you don't find what you need on this site, stop in to the office to search the index books.
Users of this FREE site must register to conduct document searches and to purchase copies. The copy fee is $1.05 per page.
To register, click HERE .
If you've already registered, log in and begin searching by clicking HERE .
Registered users can search the index, view and/or purchase document copies with a credit card.
Go to the Free Records Search website .
Enter your user name and password and click submit.
Search by Liber & Page, Name, and/or document type, etc.
NOTES When searching by name, enter last name then first, no commas.
The Both Names field means the name will be searched in both the Grantor and/or Grantee section of an indexed document. It doesn’t refer to searching for more than one person or name; e.g ., a husband and wife, A/K/As, etc.
To search for a specific document type, uncheck the box at the top where it states: “Leave this box checked to search for all document types.” When the box is unchecked, a list of document types will drop down.
Click search.
Double click on the document to view in advance or simply click “Purchase.” The indexed information appears by double clicking on a document.
Click on “Preview Image” to view the document prior to purchasing it. A low resolution image will be seen. The indexed information will still show, with the image beneath it. View the image by scrolling down the screen.
To purchase a copy, click “Add to Cart” and enter your credit/debit card information.
ROD Alert
Please be on the lookout for companies offering to help residents acquire a certified copy of their deed. These companies charge fees of $50 or more. Copies of all land records can be purchased from your ROD office for as little as $1 per page. If you're contacted by an outside company, it's advised to check with the Emmet County ROD office before buying: 231.348.1761.
FEES & SERVICES
Recording fees are payable in person via cash or check only. In office copy fees may be paid by cash or check. Online copies are payable by credit/debit card or escrow account.

E-RECORDING
The ROD office offers electronic filing, eliminating the need for paper recording of deeds, mortgages, liens and discharges of mortgages. The system is secure and electronically sends documents to the office. It permits corrections to be made back-and-forth within minutes, saving time by avoiding the mail.
Managing e-recording for the county are:
CSC (formerly known as Ingeo)
EPN
Simplifile
Contact them for guidance with the e-recording process.
LAND RECORD SEARCHES
Complete this form and bring to the office or submit to registerofdeeds@emmetcounty.org . Search results, while as accurate as the records permit, are not insured or guaranteed by the Register of Deeds Office. They are for informational purposes only.
RECORDING REQUIREMENTS
Signatures must be original ; and names must be typed or printed beneath signatures. MCLA 565.201 Sec. 1(a)
No discrepancy shall exist between the names printed in the notary acknowledgement and as printed beneath signatures. MCLA 565.201 Sec. 1(b)
When a subdivision Plat has been recorded, the lots in the Plat shall be described by the caption of the Plat & the Lot number for all purposes
MCLA 560.255
Total value ( sale price) consideration must be stated on the face of the document or a Real Estate Transfer Tax Valuation Affidavit must be attached.
MCL 207.504, 207.525
Transfer Tax shall be collected on the Total Value (sale price) consideration of the land being transferred unless exempt from either or both acts; the exemption(s) must be stated on the instrument. MCL 207.502,207.511, 207.526, 207.533
The address of the grantees in each deed of conveyance or assignment of real estate shall contain the street number address or post office address. MCLA 565.201 Sec. 1(d)
The name and address of the person who drafted the document must appear on documents executed in Michigan. MCLA 565.201a Corporation, Partnership, Trust, Association MCLA 55.265(g)
Documents purporting to convey or encumber real estate executed in Michigan require an acknowledgment by a judge, clerk of a court of record or a notary public within this state. MCLA 565.8; form: LAND 565.47, MCLA 565.265; 565.267
A certified copy of the death certificate or proof of death must be recorded or have been recorded and referenced by Liber and Page on said document when “survivor” is indicated on the document. MCLA 565.48
Court orders must be certified and sealed by the clerk of the court. MCLA 565.401; 565.411
The document submitted for recording must be legible. MCLA 565.201 Sec. 1(f) (iv) .
Documents must have a margin of unprinted space at least 2-½ inches at the top of the first page and at least ½ inch on all remaining sides of each page. MCLA 565.201 Sec. 1(f) (i)
Documents must display on the first line of print on the first page, a single statement identifying the recordable event that the instrument evidences. MCLA 565.201 Sec. 1(f) (ii) ; 565.201 Sec. 3
The type on the form must be printed with black ink; type size at least 10-point type. MCLA 565.201 Sec. 1 (f) (iii)(iv)
The paper on which the document is printed must be white and not less than 20-pound weight. MCLA 565.201 Sec. 1(f) (iv)
The size of the document and any attachment thereto must be at least 8-½ inches by 11 inches; at most 8-½ inches by 14 inches. MCLA 565.201 Sec. 1(f) (v)(vi)
Unless required by state or federal law or court order, no more than 4 sequential digits of any social security number may appear on the instrument. MCLA 565.201 Sec. 1(g)
Instruments shall not purport to evidence more than one recordable event. MCLA 565.201(3)
When a subdivision plat has been recorded, the lots in the plat shall be described by the caption of the plat and the lot number for all purposes. MCLA 560.255
If a Trust Document is presented for recording it shall be recorded as a
separate document. MCL565.434
This is intended to be a complete list but please refer to a Title Company
Attorney or State of Michigan website for further accuracy
NOTES
Self-addressed return envelopes are required.
Documents that do not meet recording requirements will be returned for correction.

HISTORY
Adopted by the United States Congress in 1835, the first constitution of the State of Michigan established the Register of Deeds as the official recording office for all legal instruments pertaining to the transfer and encumbrances of properties in each county.
